value_criterion: a concrete way to SHOW the Socratic method working (questioning that exposes a hidden assumption or contradiction) so an audience grasps how it operates; must enact questioning-to-expose, not lecture about Socrates

obvious_clusters.label: break_test
member_ideas: ask 'what would break if that were true?'
what's the smallest change that flips the answer?
remove a constraint and watch them rebuild

obvious_clusters.label: contradiction_pair
member_ideas: present two contradictory expert quotes, ask which
earlier you said X, now Y — which is it?
two conflicting student answers, which survives?

obvious_clusters.label: predict_reveal
member_ideas: predict the outcome, then show reality, ask why it failed
predict code output before running
if true, what would you expect to see?

obvious_clusters.label: counterexample
member_ideas: have them generate a counterexample to their own rule
build a toy example that yields an absurd result

obvious_clusters.label: steelman
member_ideas: steelman the opposing view first
defend against the stupidest objection
play devil's advocate against their own conclusion

obvious_clusters.label: teach_back
member_ideas: explain it to someone who knows nothing
teach it back to test real understanding

obvious_clusters.label: work_backwards
member_ideas: if that's true, what must also be true? (backwards)
give a solved problem, ask what question it answers

obvious_clusters.label: deliberate_error
member_ideas: restate their claim slightly wrong, watch them correct it
deliberately misunderstand and ask them to fix you

obvious_clusters.label: five_whys
member_ideas: keep asking 'why?' until they hit bedrock or contradict themselves

negative_fringe.landmark: lecturing ABOUT Socrates — describes, never enacts the questioning
a bare list of questioning techniques — the obvious set; classroom moves, not a demonstration medium
a formal debate — two sides ASSERTING, not questioning-to-expose
an info-seeking Q&A or interview — questions, but to gather facts, not to collapse an assumption
an abstract logic diagram with no live belief actually being tested
